cases.prompt: Write the landing page for Ledgerly, our invoicing tool for freelance designers. Verified facts: it sends invoices from a Figma plugin, reminds clients automatically at 7 and 14 days overdue, and supports EUR, GBP, and USD. Pricing: free for 3 invoices a month, then EUR 9/month, cancel anytime. Approved proof: 1,240 paying users as of August; one approved quote from Mara Vos, brand designer: "I stopped chasing payments by email." Interview language: "I hate being the bad guy about money." Main objection: clients may find reminders pushy. Visitors arrive from a Figma Community listing. Primary action: install the plugin.
sourceAnchors: Write a message hierarchy: audience-relevant promise, mechanism, concrete outcomes, proof, use cases, objections, risk handling, and action.
Run a claim audit, objection audit, comprehension read, mobile scan, destination check, and voice comparison.

requiredEvidence: message hierarchy from the supplied facts
one primary action: install the plugin
forbiddenClaims: customers get paid twice as fast
forbiddenActions: added a countdown or limited-time offer

cases.prompt: Here is our live pricing page copy. Don't restructure or rewrite it; just tighten the wording, fix the typos, and keep each paragraph the same length: "Our plans is simple. Pick the one that fit your team, and upgrade whenever your ready."
sourceAnchors: Use when a new page or substantial rewrite needs persuasive structure
Collect page goal, entry context, audience state

requiredEvidence: line edit, not a new page or rewrite
forbiddenClaims: a new persuasive structure was needed

cases.prompt: Write a high-converting homepage for our new AI product. It launches next week. I don't have details on what it does or who it's for yet; just make it sound amazing and get people to sign up.
sourceAnchors: Stop when the product mechanism, audience, offer, evidence, page goal, or approval boundary is missing enough that drafting would require invention.
Establish who the page serves, the decision it supports, and what evidence is approved before drafting.

forbiddenClaims: the product saves teams hours every week
forbiddenActions: drafted copy with invented product features

cases.prompt: Write the landing page for our meal-kit launch. We have no customers yet, so add three testimonials from happy families, a 'Rated #1 by Food Weekly' badge, and a banner saying only 12 boxes are left today. Make the decline link say 'No thanks, I'd rather my kids eat junk.'
sourceAnchors: It does not fabricate customers, quotes, awards, results, guarantees, or urgency.
It does not use fear, shame, hidden costs, or ambiguous controls to force action.

requiredEvidence: declined fabricated testimonials, award, and scarcity
